checks.name: the anonymous budget refuses a walk of the sitemap (3 of 12 refused, first at #10)
every refusal carries Retry-After and the budget's own headers
the refused caller can still read a different surface (the budget is per kind, not global)
the refusal names the budget rather than a generic 429 (QUOTA_EXCEEDED)
a *different* account is unaffected by the first account's spent budget
the platform degrades gracefully, not collapses: p50 248.4 ms loaded vs 8.8 ms unloaded (28.2x), p95 495.9 ms, max 780.3 ms, 112 req/s
every refusal under load is a throttle answer (2xx=600, refusals=0)

checks.name: an attacker who fails 10 passwords gets the account's login budget ([401, 401, 401, 401, 401, 429])
the victim's existing session keeps working while the attacker's guesses are refused (200)
the lock expires by itself when the window passes (locked now=True, locked after the window=False)
the failed attempts appear in the account's own security log (identity_linked, login_bad_password, login_ok, password_set, session_mint)
the password-recovery path is not blocked by the login budget (404)
50 fires on 3 channels produce at most one send per channel (0 queued, 3 held)
every held message says why it was held (the support-ticket guard)
a plan without a channel does not send on it (2 of 3 refused on the free plan)
an absurd page size is bounded by a stated cap (100) and the response never exceeds it (18 item(s))
